newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-KNOX LEADS ACT TO SUPER 12 SUMMIT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-KNOX LEADS ACT TO SUPER 12 SUMMIT.

text.p: Australian Capital Territory (ACT) went on a try-scoring spree on Friday to beat South Africa's Free State 50-23 and move to the top of the Super 12 rugby union tournament standings.

ACT ran in six tries to Free State's three, picking up one bonus point by scoring more than four tries to add to the four they earned for victory, to jump above both Auckland and the Gauteng Lions (formerly Transvaal). The win also stretched ACT's remarkable unbeaten home run to nine games since the tournament began last year.
Flyhalf David Knox played a major role in the victory, setting up two tries and landing four penalties and four conversions for a personal tally of 20 points.

ACT laid the foundations for their win with three tries in a blistering 15-minute period before half-time after conceding an early try from a line-out to Free State hooker Naka Drotske. Captain Brett Robinson charged over from the bottom of a ruck to level the scores at 11-11 after 25 minutes before centre James Holbeck flashed over three minutes later to finish a sparkling backline movement.
Knox made up for missing two earlier attempts at goal when he set up the best try of the half for winger Mitch Hardy five minutes from the break.
The ACT fly-half kicked across the face of Free State's goal straight into the arms of an unattended Hardy for ACT to lead 23-11 at halftime.
Knox added two penalties in as many minutes after the break and then put the result beyond question when he drew three defenders to put winger Joe Roff over.
Larkham then broke the Free State line for a try before Roff added his second midway through the second half.
The ACT forwards dominated the rucks, mauls and line-outs against a lumbering Free State pack, winning a glut of possession which allowed their backs to run at will.
Free State picked up two consolation tries in the closing minutes to make the score less lop-sided, one a penalty try and the other to winger Stephen Brink.

Australian Capital Territory - Stephen Larkham; Mitch Hardy, James Holbeck, Pat Howard, Joe Roff; David Knox, George Gregan; Troy Coker, Brett Robinson (captain), Owen Finegan, David Giffin, John Langford, Ewen McKenzie, Marco Caputo, Patricio Noriega.

Free State - Jorrie Kruger; Chris Badenhorst, Helgard Muller (captain), Brendan Venter, Stephen Brink; Jannie de Beer, Werner Swanepoel; Johan Erasmus, Jaco Coetzee, Andre Venter, Braam Els, Stuart Landman, Dougie Heymans, Naka Drotske, Os du Randt.
